t:
(a) Pursuant to the third sentence of section 7 of Public Law 473, approved June 29, 1946, all functions and responsibilities of the Personnel Division, National Headquarters, Selective Service System, established under authority of section 8 (g) of the Selective Training and Service Act of 1940, as amended, together with so much of the records of the Selective Service System, and so much of the unexpended balances of appropriations of the Selective Service System, as the Director of the Bureau of the Budget may determine to relate primarily to such functions, are hereby transferred, effective March 29, 1947, from the Selective Service System to the Secretary of Labor.
 
    (b) 
The second sentence of section 600 (a) of Public Law 346, approved June 22, 1944, is hereby amended by substituting the words “Director of the Office of Selective Service Records” for the words “Director of the National Selective Service System“.
 
    (c) Section 600 (c) of Public Law 346, approved June 22, 1944, is hereby amended by substituting the words“ Office of Selective Service Records” for the words “Veterans’ Personnel Division, National Selective Service System”.

fable.w: The section transfers functions, records, and funds from the Selective Service System to the Secretary of Labor and makes conforming name changes to an earlier law. The tempting reading is that the Budget Director's determination or the reference to a 'Director' signals consultation, but every actor is a federal official or agency. No state, tribe, expert, company, or member of the public is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue.
fable.s: are hereby transferred, effective March 29, 1947, from the Selective Service System to the Secretary of Labor.

qwen_block.w: This section describes an internal transfer of functions and records between federal agencies (the Selective Service System and the Department of Labor). It does not involve consultation, coordination, or participation with any entities outside the federal government, such as states, tribes, the public, or private organizations. The actors involved are all within the federal government.
qwen_block.s: all functions and responsibilities of the Personnel Division, National Headquarters, Selective Service System... are hereby transferred... from the Selective Service System to the Secretary of Labor.

opus.w: This section only moves functions, records and appropriations between federal agencies and makes changes to wording in an earlier law. The one discretionary decision, which records and funds to transfer, is made by the Director of the Bureau of the Budget, a federal official. No states, experts, members of the public or other outside parties are consulted, so it is not participation.
opus.s: as the Director of the Bureau of the Budget may determine to relate primarily to such functions, are hereby transferred, effective March 29, 1947, from the Selective Service System to the Secretary of Labor.
opus.b: The section transfers functions, records and money from the Selective Service System to the Secretary of Labor, and it changes the names of offices in an earlier law. The only tempting part is that the Director of the Bureau of the Budget "may determine" which records and funds go with the transfer. That decision is made entirely by a federal official. No outside party is consulted or involved.

qwen_chat.w: This section describes the transfer of functions and records from one federal entity (Selective Service System) to another (Secretary of Labor). It involves only federal agencies and officials. There is no requirement to consult or coordinate with any party outside the federal government, such as states, tribes, or the public.
qwen_chat.s: all functions and responsibilities of the Personnel Division, National Headquarters, Selective Service System... are hereby transferred... from the Selective Service System to the Secretary of Labor.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that transferring functions to the Secretary of Labor involves coordination with outside entities, but the text only describes an internal administrative transfer of records and responsibilities between federal agencies (Selective Service System to the Department of Labor). There is no mention of consulting with states, tribes, the public, or other non-federal entities. The "Director of the Bureau of the Budget" is a federal official, so their determination is internal.
